messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate on /v1/generate (model warmup failures). Triggered by 5xx spike and container restarts. Paging alice_oncall.

alice_oncall: seeing repeated node flaps on pool-gpu-12, many containers restart within seconds. First noticed ~2m ago.

sam_runtime: logs show CUDA OOM during warmup for model-xlarge-q4. Also 'deserialize: EOF' in the same stack. attaching snippets.

sam_runtime: ```
[2024-06-19T21:06:12Z] warmup: loading model-xlarge-q4 shard-3
[2024-06-19T21:06:13Z] runtime: allocate 12.1GB gpu memory
[2024-06-19T21:06:13Z] ERROR: CUDA OOM: failed to allocate 122880000 bytes
[2024-06-19T21:06:13Z] warmup: deserialization error: unexpected EOF while reading header
[2024-06-19T21:06:13Z] container: exit code 137
```

leah_mlops: confirmed artifact checksum for shard-3 is valid on disk. suspect partial read during streaming into GPU memory (maybe kernel timeout).

alice_oncall: impact? mike_cs, can you triage customer-visible errors?

mike_cs: support flags elevated 4 tickets in last 10m. Errors show 502s and model-load timeouts. Customers on Dedicated saw degraded latency; hosted customers got retries and fallback to smaller models for some routes.

nina_pm: any live mitigation we can do asap to reduce customer impact?

sam_runtime: quick mitigations in priority order:
1) Stop warmup on model-xlarge-q4 across pool-gpu-12 to prevent stampede.
2) Route new requests to model-xlarge-int8 (smaller, compatible) via smart-routing fallback.
3) Force-graceful drain of nodes with repeated OOMs.
4) If safe, restart node agents after clearing local /tmp cache.

alice_oncall: executing step 1 now: disabling warmup tag for model-xlarge-q4 in region-us-east-1. `curl -X PATCH https://controlplane/...` (run).

incident-bot: NOTE: warmup-disabled for model-xlarge-q4 in us-east-1 by alice_oncall at 21:08:45.

sam_runtime: applying routing policy change to route traffic away from model-xlarge-q4 to model-xlarge-int8 with lower concurrency. Will push canary to 10% first.

leah_mlops: suggestion: bump compile timeout for deserialization to 60s for retries; current default 20s may be too low and triggers incomplete reads when combined with OOM retries.

raj_englead: do we know if this is a driver/kernel regression? Any recent infra changes?

sam_runtime: Noted recent CUDA driver update on pool-gpu-12 two hours ago during maintenance window (driver 12.3.1). Correlates with initial flaps. Rolling back driver on one node for test.

alice_oncall: rolling restart of node gpu-12-07 to reproduce after rollback. If it stays stable we'll schedule rollback for the pool.

mike_cs: notifying impacted customers: drafted message — short ETA and workaround (route to smaller model, retries). Posting to affected accounts now.

mike_cs: "We've detected model warmup failures causing elevated errors for some inference requests. We're routing traffic to an alternate model variant and investigating. No data loss. Expect degraded latency while mitigation is in place."

sam_runtime: added temporary autoscaler throttle to prevent concurrent warmups on same node (set max_warmups_per_node=1). This should reduce memory pressure.

leah_mlops: pushing a diagnostic job to collect per-shard read latencies and kernel timeouts for the last 30m.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Faults reduced after routing change. Error rate dropped from 16% -> 3% over 5 minutes. Continue monitoring.

alice_oncall: still seeing intermittent deserialize EOFs on remaining nodes, but no container restarts after throttle applied.

raj_englead: plan for next 1h? rollback drivers if test confirms. schedule permanent increase to compile timeout and investigate streaming code path.

sam_runtime: agree. If rollback on gpu-12-07 holds for 15m we'll roll back pool driver. Longer term: add additional prefetch/backpressure to model artifact streamer and implement retry with partial-cache recovery.

nina_pm: update PM board with mitigation & customer impact. mark incident P2, since mitigation reduced errors and customers have fallback.

mike_cs: closing communication loop with customers; flagging accounts for follow-up postmortem.

alice_oncall: handoff to sam_runtime for deep dive. I'm going offline in 20m. tagging @sam_runtime for on-call takeover.

sam_runtime: taking over. collecting core dumps and full GPU memory traces. will escalate to infra if rollback needed > pool-wide.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: handoff from alice_oncall to sam_runtime recorded at 21:17:59.

sam_runtime: preliminary root cause hypothesis: driver/firmware/streaming interplay causing allocation failures during simultaneous warmups; deserializer code not resilient to mid-stream interrupts leading to EOF errors.

leah_mlops: noted. will prepare a test patch for streamer to verify atomic file reads and add retry-with-backoff.

raj_englead: thanks all. please capture timeline, config changes, customer list for postmortem. I'll join callback if needed.

mike_cs: created incident ticket INC-1729 and linked support threads.

sam_runtime: will update status in 30m or earlier if rollback needed.

incident-bot: RESOLVED? monitoring shows stable error rate under SLA thresholds for last 10m. Assigning to sam_runtime for triage and postmortem.

sam_runtime: acknowledged. starting detailed collection and will open a follow-up doc with action items (driver rollback plan, streamer fix, compile timeout bump, warmup throttling permanent guard).

mike_cs: tagging affected customers for follow-up once postmortem is ready.

alice_oncall: thanks team, good coordination.
